url.label: WAIP server URL
url.help: Base URL of the WAIP dispatch server (Socket.IO endpoint, namespace /waip is appended automatically)

monitorID.label: Monitor ID
monitorID.help: Loaded live from the configured server's /waip/ overview page - choose by Leitstelle, Kreis, Träger or Wache, or pick 'Alle Wachalarme' (ID 0) for every incident. If the server can't be reached, an ID can still be entered manually.

registrationTimeoutSec.label: Registration timeout (s)
registrationTimeoutSec.help: How long to wait for the server to confirm the monitor registration before logging a warning; the connection itself keeps running either way.

reconnectDelaySec.label: Reconnect delay (s)
reconnectDelaySec.help: Wait time before the adapter automatically reconnects after a lost connection or a connection error.

rdAlarmierungEnabled.label: Process rescue-service incidents
rdAlarmierungEnabled.help: When unchecked, incidents whose einsatzart identifies them as a rescue-service call (contains "Rettung" or "Krankentransport", case-insensitive) are ignored completely - no states are updated, no history entry is written, no TTS announcement is triggered. Useful because some WAIP dispatch centers only ever signal rescue-service incidents unreliably or not at all.

rdKeywordDecodingEnabled.label: Automatically decode rescue-service keywords (R<RTW>N<NEF>[p][f][-NT], with or without spaces)
rdKeywordDecodingEnabled.help: Rescue-service keyword scheme R<RTW>N<NEF>, optionally followed by a p/f modifier and/or an NT suffix (e.g. "R1N0" = 1 ambulance, no emergency physician). Two spellings are recognized: without a space and with a hyphen before NT (Leitstelle Lausitz, e.g. "R1N1p", "R1N0-NT") and with a space and without a hyphen (Leitstelle Brandenburg/IRLS, e.g. "R1N1 p", "R1N0 nt") - has no effect if your dispatch center doesn't use one of these patterns, since the keyword just won't match. Takes priority over the table on the Keyword descriptions tab when a keyword matches.

rdLabelR.label: Label for R (ambulance count)
rdLabelR.help: Text used in the generated description for the R<n> part, e.g. "Rettungswagen: 1".

rdLabelN.label: Label for N (emergency vehicle count)
rdLabelN.help: Text used in the generated description for the N<n> part, e.g. "Notfalleinsatzfahrzeug: 0".

rdLabelP.label: Label for suffix p (polytrauma)
rdLabelP.help: Text appended when the keyword ends in "p".

rdLabelF.label: Label for suffix f (first responder)
rdLabelF.help: Text appended when the keyword ends in "f".

rdLabelNT.label: Label for suffix -NT / nt (special ambulance transport)
rdLabelNT.help: Text appended when the keyword ends in "-NT" or " nt".

stichwortMappingHelp.text: Maps einsatz.stichwort to einsatz.beschreibung. Comparison is case-insensitive and treats spaces/hyphens as equivalent (any run of either collapses to one before comparing), so e.g. "H:VU mit P" and "H:VU-mit-P" match the same row - no need for a separate row per spelling. If several rows match, the most specific (longest) pattern wins automatically - row order has no effect on matching, sort by any column freely. Pre-filled with an example fire/rescue keyword list as a starting point - it is not confirmed to match your own dispatch center's actual keywords, edit/replace as needed. To back up or transfer this table, use ioBroker's standard instance configuration export/import (JSON). After using that import, reload the Admin page before checking this table - the open config dialog doesn't refresh it from an external import automatically (a state-sync limitation of the Admin table component itself).

mapImageEnabled.label: Generate a map image for each incident
mapImageEnabled.help: For every incident with valid coordinates, downloads OpenStreetMap tiles and composes a PNG centered on the incident's location, with the incident area WAIP-Web sends drawn as an outline (falls back to a marker dot if no area polygon is available). The file path is written to the einsatz.kartenbildPfad state, e.g. for sending as a Pushover attachment from a Blockly/JavaScript script. Only the 10 most recent images are kept, older ones are deleted automatically. Uses the public tile.openstreetmap.org server - keep this to the intended one-image-per-incident use per the OSM Tile Usage Policy.

mapImageTimeout.label: OSM timeout (s)
mapImageTimeout.help: Maximum time to wait for the map image (OSM tile download and composition) to finish before continuing to process the incident. If it isn't ready within this time, a warning is logged and einsatz.kartenbildPfad stays empty for this incident.

mapImageZoom.label: Zoom level
mapImageZoom.help: OpenStreetMap zoom level (1 = whole world, 19 = building level). Fixed zoom for the marker dot; a maximum for the polygon outline, auto-reduced if needed to keep it fully visible (see 'Show incident-area polygon').

mapImageOutlineColor.label: Marker & outline color
mapImageOutlineColor.help: Color of the marker dot, or of the polygon outline when one is drawn (see 'Show incident-area polygon').

mapImageWidth.label: Image width (px)
mapImageWidth.help: Width of the generated map image in pixels (applies to both the marker dot and the polygon outline).

mapImageHeight.label: Image height (px)
mapImageHeight.help: Height of the generated map image in pixels (applies to both the marker dot and the polygon outline).

mapImageShowPolygon.label: Show incident-area polygon
mapImageShowPolygon.help: When checked (default), the incident-area polygon WAIP-Web sends is drawn as an outline (falling back to a centered marker dot only when no polygon is available). Uncheck to always show the simple centered marker dot instead, even when a polygon is available.

mapImageOutlineThickness.label: Outline thickness (px)
mapImageOutlineThickness.help: Line thickness of the incident-area outline, in pixels.

dashboardEnabled.label: Enable dashboard
dashboardEnabled.help: Shows the last N incidents (N = number below) matching this instance's Monitor ID (Connection tab) as dashboard.einsatz1..einsatzN, correlated via the incident's dispatch center/district/carrier/station IDs, same matching logic as the Monitor ID dropdown itself. Monitor ID 0 (all dispatch monitors) shows all incidents. Disabling the feature removes the entire dashboard object tree; reducing the count below removes only the now-unused slots. Both take effect on the next adapter restart after saving.

dashboardSlotCount.label: Number of incidents to show
dashboardSlotCount.help: How many of the most recent matching incidents to show (dashboard.einsatz1..einsatzN). Higher values create proportionally more states/channels.

dashboardRefreshSec.label: Refresh interval (s)
dashboardRefreshSec.help: How often the dashboard is refreshed. A full refresh connects to the server once per slot in sequence, so it realistically takes several seconds per active slot - the minimum here reflects that.

dashboardHelp.text: Map images are derived from this adapter's own incident-map history (see 'Incident map image' tab) and are only available where it already generated one for a matching incident - most complete when Monitor ID is 0 and map images are enabled. A manual refresh can be triggered any time via the dashboard.refreshNow button state.
